cover_course: Registered Behavior Technician  ·  BACB Test Content Outline (TCO-3)
study_order: Study order. The modules are numbered in the order the training delivers them, and they build. Chapters 1–5 are the foundations — scope of practice and ethics, what ABA is, the 3-term contingency, why behavior occurs, and verbal operants — and everything after them assumes those. Chapters 6–8 cover measurement: why data matters, every data collection procedure, and how to read a graph. Chapters 9–11 prepare you, the environment, and the client, and set out the ten ethical responsibilities of Section 2. Chapters 12–15 are assessment: skill-based, preference, and functional. The long middle, chapters 16–31, is skill acquisition — instructional control and discrimination training, prompting and fading, DTT, naturalistic teaching, chaining, shaping, self-monitoring, generalization and maintenance. Chapters 32–41 are behavior reduction: BIPs, antecedent strategies, extinction and differential reinforcement, FCT, punishment, severe behavior, In Sync Engagement, and keeping your own cool. Chapters 42–47 close with documentation, communication, supervision, ethical dilemmas, and certification. Eight modules have no notes in the source manual; each one says what to do instead. The A–Z glossary at the back merges every terminology table — start there when you meet a term you don't recognise.
